Hi Brian —

Thanks for the clear ask and for sending the DPA. We can draft a concise letter that covers routing, failover windows, and oversight for subprocessors; below are the items we typically include and where we are comfortable committing today: 

1) Normal operation: customer data is routed and served from the customers requested region (US) and we will not intentionally serve production inference traffic from another region.

2) Temporary cross-hop: We support a transient failover mechanism for operational continuity. Proposed commitment: temporary cross-region processing will be limited to 72 hours per incident, unless extended by mutual written agreement. Any extension beyond 72 hours will require escalation to legal and the customers designated contact.

3) Observability & cryptography: All temporary cross-hop events will be recorded in our audit logs (timestamp, region, affected model/route, affected tenant id). Data in transit during a cross-hop will continue to be encrypted in transit and at rest; any disk or snapshot used during the hop will be wrapped with customer-managed KMS where the customer requests it.

4) Notification & evidence: Redwood will notify the designated PaxHealth contact within 24 hours of any temporary cross-hop. We will provide the subprocessor activation evidence (who, where, duration) within 72 hours of notification. If the request is for a standing escrow of the roster, we can provide a snapshot on request and a secure short-lived export for review.

5) Scope carveouts: The commitment above applies to production inference requests. Non-production workloads (e.g., test/dev) can be routed by policy and are not covered by this regional routing guarantee unless explicitly agreed.

Ill draft the letter and share a one-page draft by EOD tomorrow. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Karthik (ops) for quick confirmation on the logging retention and the feasibility of the 72-hour evidence SLA.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Security & Trust | Redwood Inference
